desc:
Each interval [start, end) is half-open and covers every moment t with start ≤ t < end. You want to delete some intervals so that no moment is covered by more than k of the remaining intervals.

Return the minimum number of intervals you must delete. (With k = 1 this is the classic problem of making the intervals non-overlapping.)

intervals = [[1, 3], [2, 4], [3, 5]], k = 1  ->  1
intervals = [[1, 10], [2, 9], [3, 8], [4, 7]], k = 2  ->  2

In the first example removing [2, 4) leaves two touching intervals. In the second example all four intervals share the moment 4, so two of them must go.
hints: Think of the intervals in order of start time. At the moment a new interval starts, how many kept intervals are still running?
If after adding the new interval more than k kept intervals are running, one of them has to go. Deleting the one that ends latest frees the most future time.
Keep a min-heap of end times to forget finished intervals and a max-heap (with lazy deletion) to find the running interval with the latest end. Count each eviction.
editorial: Sort the intervals by start and sweep. Maintain the set of kept intervals that are still running. When an interval starts, first drop the kept intervals that ended (end ≤ start), then add the new one. If the running count now exceeds k, evict the running interval with the largest end (this may be the new interval itself) and count one removal. After the eviction exactly k are running, so one eviction per step suffices.

The greedy choice is optimal by an exchange argument: all running intervals are alive right now, so any of them is equally harmful at this moment; the one that ends latest can only cause more overlap later, so removing it never hurts compared to removing another. This is the same idea as the optimal greedy for k = 1 that keeps intervals with the earliest ends.

Implementation: a min-heap on end times expires finished intervals, and a max-heap on end times finds the eviction candidate; an inactive flag per interval makes deletions lazy in both heaps. Each interval is pushed and popped O(1) times: O(n log n) time, O(n) space.
solution:
import heapq


def minRemovalsToCap(intervals, k):
    order = sorted(range(len(intervals)), key=lambda i: intervals[i][0])
    inactive = [False] * len(intervals)
    by_end = []   # min-heap (end, id): expires finished intervals
    by_late = []  # max-heap (-end, id): finds the eviction candidate
    running = 0
    removed = 0
    for i in order:
        s, e = intervals[i]
        while by_end and by_end[0][0] <= s:
            _, j = heapq.heappop(by_end)
            if not inactive[j]:
                inactive[j] = True
                running -= 1
        heapq.heappush(by_end, (e, i))
        heapq.heappush(by_late, (-e, i))
        running += 1
        if running > k:
            while inactive[by_late[0][1]]:
                heapq.heappop(by_late)
            _, j = heapq.heappop(by_late)
            inactive[j] = True
            running -= 1
            removed += 1
    return removed
